requirements: Create each ClientChannel before launching its bridge in a fresh non-nested run directory.
Use independent client JVMs with different player UUIDs and game directories.
Server process is externally supervised; record PID and creation time, logs, world path and source/artifact hashes.
Wait for server readiness and each client ready event; both state snapshots must identify the two connected players.
Provision actor with minecraft:bat through the server fixture or operator command before selection.
Do not interpret completed command events as successful server execution.

steps.oracle: Actor and observer detail.players entries for actor UUID report form minecraft:bat.
Both snapshots report actor form minecraft:bat and showNameTag false.
Distinct framebuffer artifacts exist under each role directory; image contents require separate visual validation.

steps.lifecycle: Stop actor client, observe process exit, launch fresh actor client channel with same player UUID and game directory.
steps.oracle: Both snapshots regain actor form minecraft:bat and showNameTag false.

steps.lifecycle: Stop clients and dedicated server cleanly; observe each process exit; start a new server process using the same world; launch fresh channels for both clients.
steps.oracle: Different server process identity and observed old exit, then both snapshots show persisted actor form minecraft:bat and showNameTag false.

limitations: This specification is not a recorded gameplay pass.
Client appearance snapshots demonstrate received client state, not visible framebuffer replacement or authoritative server save contents.
The session runner must supply lifecycle callbacks, fixtures and server readiness evidence before reconnect or restart can execute.
Late tracking, dimension travel, death, visible nametag rendering and simultaneous background focus isolation require additional live scenarios.
